delta: # Story 72 — Long conversation thread p

ages on the desk screen (Story: CRM-107)

## Prerequisites

- `CONVERSATION-1-API` shipped — the desk thread endpoint returns a
paged window (page/pageSize/total or nextCursor). Coordinate with `CONVERSATION-4-API (CRM-106)` for

the exact wire shape; do not add filtering the API does not expose.
- Sibling fr
ontend paging precedents already merged: `web/src/pages/portal/MyTicketsPage.tsx` (+ `useMyTickets.ts`) and `web
/src/pages/tickets/TicketHistory.tsx` (+ `useTicketHistory.ts`). This story follows the **API's window, not the screen's** convention those files established.

---

## Story Goal

A long ticket conversation thread in the desk (agent-facing `TicketThread`) is paged on screen using the API's window — the screen never asks for more than
one page at a time, never concatenates all pages into an unbounded list, and never re-implements ordering, fil

tering, or sizing the API already owns (BR-4).

Because the thread is ordered **oldest-first**, the reader who opens a long th
read almost always wants the **newest** message. The screen therefore lands on the **last page** by default, with a visible reason (e.g. a "newest first" affordance / pa
ging control that shows which page you are on and lets you page back through history). Every visible string comes from `en.

ts` and `ar.ts` (BR-6).

Explicitly out of scope: any change under `api/` — those belong to `CONVERSATION-4-API (C

RM-106)`.

---

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketThread.tsx` — the desk thread component that ren
ders the message list. Identify where messages are pulled (`useTicketThread`) and rendered. This is the file to convert from "render everything the

hook returned" to "render one page and expose a pager".
2. `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketThread.ts` — current hook. Confirm its request
shape (`request(...)`, `useRequest` state machine `idle | loading | success | error`). This is the hook to extend with page/window hand

ling.
3. `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketThread.css` — where the pager / paging control styles belong.
4. `web/src/pages/tickets
/TicketThread.test.tsx` — the pattern to extend (fetch stub, Testing Library queries, i18n rendering). Match its

render harness exactly, including `stub-me` (a desk screen mounts the shell).
5. `web/src/pages
/portal/MyTicketsPage.tsx` and `web/src/pages/portal/useMyTickets.ts` — reference implementation for reading the API's window (page/pageSize/total) and rendering "Page

X of Y" plus previous/next controls without inventing local pagination.
6. `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketHistory.tsx` and `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketH

istory.ts` — the other precedent: "the answer says what it gave and from where, and the screen only asks for the next one."
7. `web/src/shared/hooks/useRequest.ts`
— the four-state hook. Do **not** invent a second request shape; keep `fields`-carrying errors int

act.
8. `web/src/shared/api/client.ts` and `web/src/shared/api/base-url.ts` — `request(path)` already prefixes `/api/v1`; do not double-prefix when

adding paging query params.
9. `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` — the nested one-level
camelCase leaves. All new pager strings must land in both files in the **same edit** or `web/src/sh

ared/i18n/parity.test.ts` fails.
10. `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` — the guard that catches literal JSX strings (including separators typed between tags).
11. `web/src/testing/stub-me.ts`

— mount helper for desk screens.
12. `web/src/testing/render.tsx` — the render harness the existing thread test uses.
13. `.
squad/plan-lessons.md` — read first. In particular the lessons on paging, on `Response`
-per-call fetch stubs (L-30), on bidi isolates for interpolated values (L-51), and on never wi

ring a route only its author can navigate to.
14. Grep for `useTicketThread` under `web/src/pages/tickets/` to enumerate every call site before

changing the hook's return shape.
15. Grep for `pageSize`, `nextCursor`, `total`, and `page` inside `web/src/pages/portal/useMyTickets.ts

` and `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketHistory.ts` to copy the exact field names the API layer already uses.

---

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current:** `TicketThread` renders
whatever the thread endpoint returned in one pass. On a long thread this either blows past the API window silently or presents the oldest mess

ages first with no way to reach the newest.
- **New (BR-4):** the screen displays exactly one API page at a time; page size and
ordering are the API's; the screen adds no client-side sort or filter. A pager surfaces `Page X of Y` and previ
ous/next controls. The initial landing page is the **last** page (newest messages), and the UI names why ("Showing new

est — page X of Y", both languages).
- **New (BR-6):** no literal user-visible strings in
JSX; every label, aria-label, and separator text lives in `en.ts`/`ar.ts` under a new nested group (e.g. `

ticketThread.pager`).

---

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Extend `useTicketThread` to consume the API's window

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketThread.ts`

- Accept a `page` arg
ument (1-indexed) and optionally `pageSize` **only if** the endpoint accepts them; otherwise pass through wh
atever cursor field the API layer defined in `CONVERSATION-4-API (CRM-106)`. Use the exact query-parameter names the API cont

ract publishes — grep `useMyTickets.ts` / `useTicketHistory.ts` for the naming convention already in use before adding new ones.
- Keep the `useRequest` four-state cont

ract. The success payload the hook exposes must include:
  - `messages` — the page's items in

the order the API returned them (do not re-sort on the client).
  - `page`, `pageSize`, `total` (or the cursor equivalents the

API uses).
  - `totalPages` — derive from `total` / `pageSize` **only** when `total` is present; otherwise expose the cursor fields verbatim.
- Do

**not** merge pages into a growing array. Each page load replaces the previous window (the API's window, not the screen's).
- Do

**not** call `request()` with a hard-coded `/api/v1` prefix (`shared/api/base-url.ts` already prefixes it).

### 2 — Render one page with a pager in `TicketTh

read`

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketThread.tsx`

- On first mount for a given ticket, request the **last** page: fetch page 1 first only
to learn `total`/`totalPages`, then request `totalPages` — **or**, preferred, add a `?page=last
` shortcut in the hook that resolves to the last page in a single request if the API sup

ports it. Choose whichever the API contract from CRM-106 exposes; do not invent one.
- Render exactly the messages in `

messages` for the current page. Do not append; do not sort; do not filter.
- Add a pager control below (or above, matching the RTL/LTR conventions already used

in `MyTicketsPage.tsx`) with:
  - "Previous" button — disabled when `page === 1`.
  - "Next" button — disabled when `page === totalPages`.
  - A status line: `"Show

ing newest — page {page} of {totalPages}"` when landed on the last page; `"Page {page} of {totalPages}"` on any other page.
- All numeric values
interpolated into a translated sentence must be wrapped with the bidi isolate helper used by `pages/tickets/history-sentence.ts` (U+2068 … U+2069, L

-51).
- Preserve existing loading and error states via `useRequest`'s `idle | loading | success | error` machine. Reuse `t.errors[code]` **
only** after reading the shared sentence; if the shared one misreads the situation (e.g. a 404 on a paged-

past-the-end request), add a thread-specific sentence in `en.ts`/`ar.ts` rather than reusing a wrong default.

### 3 — Wire

the way in

- If any test or route currently loads `TicketThread` at page 0 or
with all messages, update it to match the new default (last-page landing) so the desk agent's normal navigation reaches the newest message in one

click — a route only its author can navigate to is a route that does not exist.
- Grep for `useTicketThread` callers; update each to pass the new `page` argument (or the "

last page" sentinel), and ensure the paging control is visible on the parent screen — not hidden behind a scroll or a modal footer.

### 4 — i18n keys (B

R-6)

**Files:** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`

Add, in the **same commit**, a nested group under

'
    next: 'Next',                // ar: 'التالي'
    pageOfTotal: 'Page {page} of {total}',
    showingNewest: 'Showing newest — page {page} of {total}',
    empty: 'No messages in this thread y

; interpolation is done at the call site by splicing the value with a bidi isolate wrapper, as `history-sentence.ts` does.
- The separator "—
" between the two clauses of `showingNewest` must live inside the resource string, **not** typed between JSX tags (or `pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.

ts` will fail).

### 5 — No native validators / no browser-owned rules

- The pager uses buttons, not `

<input type="number" min max>`. Do not let the browser own the "which page is valid" rule.

---

## Ed

ge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Single-page thread (`totalPages === 1`).** Render the messages; hide (or disable and label

) both pager buttons; status line reads `Page 1 of 1`. Enforced in `TicketThread.tsx` pager render branch.
- **Empty thread (`total === 0`).** Render the

`ticketThread.pager.empty` string; do not render the pager. Enforced in `TicketThread.tsx`.
- **Reader pages past the end** (e.g. race with a
message being deleted server-side). The API returns 404 or an empty page — show a thread-specific sentence and a "Go to newest" action that jumps back to `

totalPages`. Do not reuse a generic `t.errors[404]` that reads as "not found" for the whole ticket.
- **
Ticket has grown while the reader was on an old page.** `totalPages` has moved. When Next is clicked, re-request; if the
returned `page` no longer matches what was asked for, trust the API's `page` field and update the pager, not the local

intent.
- **RTL (Arabic).** Previous/Next visual order follows the document direction that `shared/i18n/index.tsx` already s

ets. Do not mirror with CSS transforms (`no-mirrored-styles.test.ts` will catch it).
- **Interpolated page numbers in Arabic sentence

.** Wrap the numeric value in U+2068 … U+2069 (L-51) so the digits do not scramble the surrounding text.
- **Fetch stub in
tests.** Every stubbed request must build a **fresh** `Response` per call (L-30) — a shared `Response` cannot be read twice,

and paging tests read it many times.
- **Desk-shell dependency.** `TicketThread` mounts inside the desk shell, which as

ks `/me`; every test must stub `/me` via `src/testing/stub-me.ts` or the shell fails to render.
- **API contract drift.** If CRM-106
exposes cursors instead of `page`/`total`, the pager's status sentence changes ("Newer messages ›" / "

‹ Older messages") — resolve by reading the CRM-106 plan and matching its field names. Do not hard-code assumptions.

---

## Test Plan

1

. **`web/src/pages/tickets/TicketThread.test.tsx`** (extend):
   - `renders the last page by default on a multi-page thread`
— stub `/api/v1/tickets/:id/messages` with a `total` of, say, 47 across pageSize 20; assert the r

endered messages are the ones from page 3, and the status line reads `Showing newest — page 3 of 3` (English) and its Arabic parity string.
   - `previ
ous button loads the page before` — click Previous; assert a second fetch was made for `page=2`; assert the rendered messages are the page-

2 fixture; status line now `Page 2 of 3`.
   - `previous is disabled on page 1; next is disabled on last page` — assert `aria-disabled` / `disabled` on the corre

ct button per state.
   - `single-page thread hides the pager` — stub `total: 3`, `pageSize: 20`; assert neither Prev nor Next

is queryable, empty-state string is not shown.
   - `empty thread shows the empty resource string` — stub `total: 0`; assert `ticketThread.pager.empty` ren

ders and no pager buttons.
   - `paging past the end shows a thread-specific message and a jump-to-newest action` — stub second click of Next to a 404; assert the

custom sentence, click the action, assert the last page loads.
   - `Arabic locale interpolates page numbers with bidi isolate` — render with Arabic;

assert the `\u2068` / `\u2069` bracket the numeric fragment.
   - Every fetch stub uses a fresh `new Response(...)` per call (L-30) and `stub-me.

ts` is invoked in `beforeEach`.
2. **`web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts`** — auto-passes once both `en.ts` and `ar.ts` carry the new `ticketThread.pager.

*` leaves in the same edit. No new test needed; verify it stays green.
3. **`web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`** — auto-runs; ensure any separator (`—`,

`·`) lives inside resource strings, not between JSX tags.
4. **`web/src/shared/i18n/no-mirrored-styles.test.ts`** — verify no new

CSS transform mirror was introduced for RTL.
5. Do **not** add or modify any test under `api/`.

---

## Migration / Rollback

- No schema change; fe
ature is purely UI + hook. Rollback = revert the `TicketThread.tsx`, `useTicketThread.ts`, `TicketThread.css`, `en.ts`, `ar.ts`, and test

edits in one commit. No data on disk changes.
- Half-applied risk: shipping the
hook change without the pager UI would silently drop older messages. Ship the two together; guard with the new test in item 1

.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend runs:** `cd web && npm test -- TicketThread` — all new and existing th

read tests green.
2. **Frontend runs:** `cd web && npm test` — full vitest suite green (parity, no-hardcoded-

strings, no-mirrored-styles included).
3. **Frontend builds:** `cd web && npm run build` — `tsc -b && vite build` succeeds. A change only vitest has

seen is not verified.
4. **Backend regression:** `cd api && npm test` — must remain green; this story does not touch `api/` and any change there

indicates an accidental edit.
5. **Regression — no AI attribution anywhere:** `git grep -nE -i "(cla
ude|copilot|chatgpt|openai|anthropic|ai[- ]assist)" -- . ':!*.l

ock'` returns no matches in modified files.
6. **Manual smoke:** run `cd api && npm start` in one shell and `cd web && npm run dev` in another; open a
ticket with > 1 page of messages as an agent; confirm the screen lands on the last page, the status line names it, Prev/Next work, and Arabic reads

correctly (digits stay attached to the correct clause).

---

## Done Criteria

- [ ] A long thread renders exactly one API page of

messages; there is no client-side concatenation, sort, or filter.
- [ ] The screen lands on the last page by default and states in words that this is the newest —

in both English and Arabic (BR-6).
- [ ] Previous/Next paging controls are visible on the desk `TicketThread` and correctly disable

at the ends.
- [ ] `ticketThread.pager.*` keys exist in both `en.ts` and `ar.ts`; `parity.test.ts` and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts

` are green.
- [ ] Interpolated page numbers are wrapped with U+2068 / U+2069 (L-51).
- [ ] `useTicketThread` uses `useRequest`'s four-state mach

ine and does not double-prefix `/api/v1`.
- [ ] All `TicketThread` tests use a fresh `Response` per fetch call (L-30) and stub `/me` (`stub-me.ts`).
- [ ] `

cd web && npm test` and `cd web && npm run build` both succeed; `cd api && npm test` unchanged and green.
- [ ] No file under `api/` was modified in this change.
- [ ] No commit,

doc, or ignore-file entry references AI assistance.
